page_title: On Tetris and Reimplementation - Stephen Brennan

summary.title: On Tetris and Reimplementation
summary.one_liner: Learn how the author built a Tetris clone in C using ncurses, with game logic separated from the UI, and why reimplementing existing programs is valuable for learning.
takeaways: Keep game rules (tetris.c) separate from the user interface (main.c), exposing only a small header API such as tg_tick().
Use ncurses to draw a grid-based interface in the terminal, which suits grid games like Tetris better than plain console I/O or a full GUI toolkit.
Each game tick processes gravity, then user input, then line clearing and scoring, and returns whether the game is still running.
Reimplementing well-known programs (games, shells, regex engines, web servers) is a practical way to build programming skill and domain knowledge.
summary.summary: The author describes writing a Tetris clone in C over roughly a day, using the ncurses library for a terminal interface. The game logic lives in tetris.c, with a tg_tick() function that handles gravity, player moves, line clearing and scoring, while main.c handles display and input in a loop. The post lists implemented features such as hold, a scoring system, levels, pause and boss-mode screens, and save/load, and notes that sound was not implemented. It closes with an argument that reimplementing existing software is a valuable way to learn.
